name: Dhairyashil Shinde
position: Software Engineer at Cal.com, GSoC'25 Rocket Chat
short_biography: Software engineer at Cal.com building open-source scheduling platform. Did Google Summer of Code last year with Rocket.Chat, where I built an AI-powered chat automation app. Before that, worked closely with billing software used by top banks and healthcare companies.
long_biography:
I started my career at RIA Advisory, where I worked on billing software for major banks and healthcare companies. That's where I learned how to build strong and scalable backend systems.

A turning point came when I created a WhatsApp bot for my own restaurant business. It made me realize how much I enjoy building tools that solve real problems.

While improving my coding skills, I came across Google Summer of Code. Rocket.Chat, with its TypeScript and React stack, felt like a great fit for me.

I contributed a lot to their embedded chat and AI apps, got selected, and built an AI-powered chat automation app. I successfully completed the program and kept contributing even after it ended.

My open-source work helped me connect with YC startups and larger open-source projects. That's how I eventually joined Cal.com, where I now work on scheduling systems.

name: Vipin Chaudhary
short_biography: Software engineer at Plane. GSoC contributor turned mentor.
long_biography:
I'm a software engineer working at Plane, contributing to an open-source project management platform. After my GSoC journey with Rocket.Chat, I continued in open source and now also mentor contributors.

My work focuses on editor workflows, developer experience, and exploring how AI can improve real-world tools.

name: Rohit Bansal
short_biography: I’m a React Native developer and Trainee Mobile Engineer at Rocket.Chat. I was a Google Summer of Code contributor, where I worked on implementing end-to-end testing using Maestro to improve app stability and developer confidence.
long_biography:
I started with open source out of curiosity and a desire to work on real-world projects. I was not initially aiming for Google Summer of Code, but through consistent contributions, I got the opportunity to be part of it with Rocket.Chat. During this time, I worked on end-to-end testing using Maestro, focusing on improving reliability and developer workflows.

I am someone who learns by building. I experiment a lot, break things, fix them, and come out with a better understanding each time. I pay attention to details, care about code quality, and enjoy writing systems that are both efficient and readable.

I learn by building and contributing. I enjoy exploring how things work, improving them, and sharing that knowledge through code. Open source has shaped my journey, and today I am part of the Rocket.Chat team.

name: Abhinav Kumar
long_biography: Former GSoC mentee turned Rocket.Chat contributor, passionate about transforming ideas into reality through code. When I'm not coding, you can find me exploring the world.
